sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Crawford County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Deeds for Crawford County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds Office, 200 W. Michigan Avenue in Grayling. The clerk and the register of deeds are a combined office here, one of 31 Michigan counties that operate that way, and the register's phone is (989) 348-2841.

The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closes from noon to 1:00 p.m. for lunch. No appointment is needed. Payment is by cash, check, money order or credit card, and the card carries a service fee.

You can also mail a document with a self-addressed stamped envelope and a check or money order payable to Crawford County or Crawford County ROD. Electronic recording comes through three vendors: CSC, Indecomm and Simplifile. The county says Simplifile is the only one that can submit anything needing a tax certification, which matters for a deed on a home sale.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Crawford County?
sections.html:
Every document costs $30 to record in Crawford County, whatever its length. The county's register page explains that Public Acts 224 through 232 of 2016 set the flat fee effective October 1, 2016, and $4 of each fee goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund.

Fees quoted by the Crawford County register of deeds page
ServiceAmount
Record any document$30.00
Assign or discharge more than one instrument$3.00 for each added instrument
Tax certification for a warranty deed$5.00, paid with the recording fee
Certify a recorded document$5.00
Copies$1.00 per page
Online search through Tapestry$8.95 per name or legal description

The $5 tax certification does not need a separate check to the treasurer. Include it in the single payment you hand the register.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a seller pay in Crawford County?
sections.html:
A Crawford County seller pays $3.75 in state tax and $0.55 in county tax for each $500 of sale value or fraction of it. The county register states both rates, and MCL 207.504 confirms the county rate for counties under 2,000,000 people.

Take a $160,000 sale. It divides into 320 units of $500, so the state tax is $1,200 and the county tax is $176, for $1,376 in all. Crawford County's median owner-occupied home value is $163,000 on the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures, so that example sits close to a typical house here.

  • The tax falls on the seller or grantor, and stamps are bought only in the county where the land lies.
  • If land sits in more than one county, the deed must split the price by county and tax goes to each.
  • A deed must state the total consideration on its face, or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit must be filed. The affidavit carries no filing fee.
  • Exemptions must be written on the face of the deed. They include consideration under $100, deeds in foreclosure or in lieu, and a quitclaim that only corrects a title flaw.

Under the state act at MCL 207.526, a conveyance from a person to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild is also exempt from state tax. The county act lists no matching exemption, so confirm the county share with the register before closing.

sections.h2: Which deeds need a tax certificate in Crawford County?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, any deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract, and an assignment of a land contract with a warranty clause all need one. MCL 211.135 requires the register to refuse the paper until the treasurer's certificate is attached.

The certificate speaks to tax liens and tax titles against the parcel and to whether taxes were paid for the five preceding years. The Crawford County Treasurer's office is at 200 W. Michigan Ave in Grayling, with the same hours as the register, and its phone is (989) 344-3231. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excepted from the requirement.

For delinquent tax on a Crawford County parcel, the treasurer's page says payments moved to a new system on November 4, 2025, with online, text-to-pay, digital wallet, ACH and autopay options. Fees apply to that system. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What makes Crawford County different for a house seller?
sections.html:
Crawford County is a small northern Lower Peninsula county where Grayling is the only incorporated community. The county has six townships plus the city, and over 75% of its roughly 360,000 acres belongs to the State of Michigan, the U.S. Forest Service or the Department of Military Affairs, per the county's history page.

The Census Bureau counted 12,988 people in 2020 and estimates 13,722 for July 2025, a 5.7% rise. Density is 23.3 people per square mile. Some 28.6% of residents are 65 or older, and 79.6% of occupied homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $862, and only 27 building permits were issued in 2025.

The county was created in 1840 as Shawono County and renamed in 1843, and county government was organized in 1879. Lumbering drove early growth, and fishing on the Au Sable River and tourism followed. Median household income is $60,392 and 14.4% of people live below the poverty line.

sections.h2: How do Crawford County sellers protect their title records?
sections.html:
The register offers a free property fraud alert service that notifies subscribers by email or phone when a document is recorded against their name. Property fraud means someone files a false document to look like the owner of a parcel, and an alert gives an early warning that would otherwise go unnoticed.

Land records can be searched on public computers in the office. Online, Tapestry is offered for occasional users and Laredo for professional subscribers. The register's files reach back to 1879, the year the county was organized. The office keeps a copy or image of each document and does not hold the original deed; the recorded instrument is stamped with a liber number.

The office does not prepare documents or answer legal questions. For a deed, the county suggests an attorney who knows Michigan real property law, a local title company, or a blank deed from an office supply store. It cautions that blank deeds found online may not meet Michigan recording rules.

sections.h2: What should I check before a Crawford County closing?
sections.html:
Work through a short list with whoever handles your closing, and settle each item before the deed goes to Grayling.

  • Ask the closing agent whether the deed carries a warranty covenant, since that triggers the tax certificate.
  • Confirm the figure for state and county transfer tax and who will purchase the stamps.
  • Check that the legal description matches the prior deed and the drafter's name and address appear.
  • Ask the treasurer whether any delinquent tax must be cleared from proceeds.
  • Plan to file the transfer paperwork with the local assessor, and for a seller who claimed the principal residence exemption, a rescission effective the closing date.

Rural parcels often involve a well, a septic system or a private road. Ask the county health and road authorities what they will want to see, because the register of deeds only handles the recorded paper.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Crawford County?
faqs.a: It costs $30 per document. A warranty deed adds a $5 tax certification, and an assignment or discharge covering more than one instrument adds $3 for each extra instrument.

faqs.q: What are the transfer tax rates in Crawford County?
faqs.a: The state rate is $3.75 and the county rate is $0.55 for each $500 of value or fraction of it. The seller pays both, and the stamps are bought in Crawford County.

faqs.q: Is the Crawford County register of deeds open at lunch?
faqs.a: No. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closes daily from noon to 1:00 p.m. No appointment is required.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed electronically in Crawford County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts documents from CSC, Indecomm and Simplifile. Simplifile is the only one of the three that can submit anything needing a tax certification.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need a tax certificate?
faqs.a: No, if it has no covenants of warranty. MCL 211.135 excepts that kind of deed. A warranty deed, a land contract and a land contract assignment with warranty language do need one.
